We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{3}⁡(2x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\ {v}^{′}=\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=-\frac{1}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{log}_{3}⁡(2x)}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{3}⁡(2x)\cdot (-\frac{1}{x})-\int (-\frac{1}{x})(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{{log}_{3}⁡(2x)}{x}-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int -\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{{log}_{3}⁡(2x)}{x}-\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)+1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{3}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.$
